text: Omar is a cook, and his hands were covered in flour. He called out to his phone, "Would you please take a picture of the bread on the counter? I want to send it to my sister, and she will only believe I baked it if she can see the crust up close." The phone understood that Omar wanted a close photo of the loaf. It opened the camera, zoomed in on the golden top, and took the picture. Omar said, "Now send it to Lena." The phone sent the photo to his sister and told him it was done. A fraction of a minute later, Lena wrote back with three happy faces. Omar grinned and wiped the flour off his hands.

They want the music to be quieter.
Turn it down.
Quieter, please.
A bit lower, thanks.
My ears hurt.
It's too loud in here for me to think.
We are about to cut the cake, so could you make the songs softer?
I can't hear Dad over the music.
Could you start something chilly and slow, and keep it very quiet in the background?
The baby is sleeping, so would you mind making it much softer?

They want the computer to restart.
Restart it.
Reboot now.
Turn it off and on.
The screen froze, can you start it over?
My laptop is stuck. It sounds like it is ringing, so please shut it down and bring it back.
I just got a new update and it says it needs a fresh start.
It has been slow all day, like old bread, so please give it a restart.
Could you please restart this computer when you have a moment?

Person: Remind me to go to the post office on Tuesday.
Assistant: Sure. What time on Tuesday?
Person: Ten in the morning. No wait, make it eleven. The kids have a late start that day.
Assistant: Okay, I set a reminder for eleven on Tuesday morning for the post office.
Person: Can you tell me if the parking is good there?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't check parking spots. I can only set the reminder.
Person: That's fine. My daughter had to design a card for her teacher, so I need to mail it anyway.
Assistant: Nice. Your reminder is ready for Tuesday at eleven.

Priya had just moved to a new city, and her hotel room was almost empty of her things. She had only one bag. She said to her phone, "I need a room for twenty-five nights near the train station. Something quiet, please." The assistant understood that she wanted a long stay close to the station. It looked at the hotels near the station and found a quiet one. It told her the room had a small desk with a drawer and a good bed. Priya asked it to draw up a short list of the three best choices, and the assistant showed her all three. She picked the first one, and the assistant booked it for twenty-five nights.

Jonas was a student with a small kitchen and a big appetite. He asked his speaker, "How long do I bake chicken and potatoes together? I want something tasty, but I'm in a hurry." The speaker understood that Jonas wanted one pan of chicken and potatoes, and that he had little time. It told him the total cooking time was about forty minutes at a hot oven. Then it said he could skip peeling the potatoes to save time. Jonas set the oven to the right heat and cut the potatoes into small pieces. The speaker started a timer for twenty-five minutes, then another for the last fifteen. When the food was done, it smelled wonderful.

Dana was a busy parent, and the car was waiting at school. She said to her phone, "I need a ride home for me and two kids, and please, not the big van. I hate when the heat is turned up too high. My daughter's seat belt is loose in my car, so I don't want to drive." The phone understood three things: she needed a ride for three people, she did not want a van, and she wanted the car to be cool. It booked a small car, wrote a note to keep the air cool, and told her the driver would arrive in six minutes at the school gate. Dana waved at the kids and waited.

name: sports_results
does: Looks up the latest score or result for a team or a sport.
inputs: the team or sport, and the day if it matters
people say:
- Who won on Sunday?
- Did the Reds lose again?
- Is the snowy game still on tonight?
- Did the rain wipe out the match?
- What was the score of the hockey game?
- How did the city team do last night?

Ben was a student who had slept very little, and he was late for class. He grabbed his car keys and said to his phone, "The front tyre looks soft. Can you do a quick check on how much air it needs?" The phone understood that Ben wanted the right tyre pressure for his car. It said the tyres should have a little more air, about five points more than they had now. Then it showed a map of the closest gas station. Ben rubbed his face, drove there, and filled the tyre. He told the phone to remind him next week to look again, and the phone said it would.

name: fridge_check
does: Tells you what food is left at home and what is running low.
inputs: the food or the place to look, like the fridge or a cupboard
people say:
- Do we still have eggs?
- I'm sick, is there any soup left?
- Is anything left in the vegetable bin?
- Are we out of milk again?
- Translate my voice notes into a list of what we need.
- What's in the fridge right now?

Person: Wake me up early and play some quiet rain sounds tonight.
Assistant: Happy to. What time should I wake you?
Person: Six. The van picks me up at seven, and I have a huge meeting at work.
Assistant: Okay. Rain sounds will play tonight, and your alarm is set for six. Should the rain sounds stop after an hour?
Person: Yes, an hour is good.
Assistant: Done. The rain sounds will stop after one hour, and I'll wake you at six.

Bread dough needs warmth, time and a little care. When people bake, they follow a recipe, but they also change things. A cold kitchen makes dough rise slowly, and a warm one makes it rise faster. On a cloudy, damp day, dough can feel stickier. Some bakers put a pan of hot water in the oven, a kind of steam bath, so the crust stays crisp. People ask for changes in simple words. They say, "Set a timer for one hour," "Make the oven hotter," or "How long until it's ready?" Most of the time, a cook just wants the dough to be soft and the crust to be golden.

A thermostat keeps a home at the heat people like. You pick a number, and the heating works until the room reaches it, then it stops. A radiator or a small heater may glow or feel hot to the touch. Many people use only a few settings, like warm in the morning and cooler at night. When they want a change, they say, "Make it warmer," "It's freezing in here," or "Turn the heat down to twenty." Some say, "Keep the bedroom cozy tonight." All of these ask for the same kind of thing: a different temperature in a room at a certain time.

name: set_pickup_spot
does: Saves a place where a driver should meet you for your ride.
inputs: the address or a landmark, and a name for it if you want to keep it
people say:
- Pick me up outside Pepper Street Cafe.
- Save this corner as my usual spot.
- Meet me at the same place as last time.
- Tell the driver to wait by the blue gate.
- I'll be at the back door of the station.

They want ideas for a birthday present for their mother.
Gift ideas for Mom?
What should I get my mother?
I need a present, quick.
Give me a single good idea for a gift under thirty dollars.
My mom loves tea and gardens. What would she like?
She turns sixty this week and I have no clue what to buy.
Could you please message me a few gift ideas for my mother? I have to order by midnight, or the present won't arrive in time for her birthday.
I'm stuck. Any thoughts on what a person who has everything might like?

Mei worked in an office, and she had a cough that would not go away. Late in the evening she said to her smart speaker, "Tomorrow at seven, please turn on the desk lamp in my bedroom, but make it dim. I want a soft start." The speaker understood that Mei wanted one lamp, with low brightness, at seven in the morning. It set the lamp for seven, at a low level. At that point Mei said, "That's the final thing for tonight." The speaker said the lamp was ready and that the light would come on at seven tomorrow. Mei drank some water, and went to sleep.

They want to know how long to boil an egg.
how long to boil eggs
boil time for an egg?
hw long do i cook a hard egg
clear answer please, how many minutes for soft eggs?
My grey old pot is on the stove. How long should the eggs stay in?
I'm in a rush, my shirt collar is already wet from the steam. When are the eggs done?
Could you tell me how long to leave eggs in boiling water so the middle stays soft?

They want the pool water to be a bit cooler.
Make the pool cooler.
Cool the water down a bit.
Subtract two degrees from the pool tomorrow at seven.
It's too hot to swim. Could you fix that by tomorrow at seven?
The birthday cake party is in the pool area tomorrow at seven, so it would be great if the water were a little colder by then.
Please lower the heat of the pool before seven tomorrow morning.
I like it chilly. Can you cool the pool before we swim?

They want to move a meeting to a different time.
Move my meeting to tomorrow at seven.
Change the time of the cooking class.
Push the ingredient shopping meeting to Friday at ten.
I put the wrong time, can you fix it? Make it tomorrow at seven.
Make the meeting later.
My phone will buzz at three, but I want the meeting at four instead.
Could you please move my call with Sam from Monday at nine to Tuesday at nine? I have a dentist visit.
Shift it by an hour.

They want the front door to lock at a certain time.
Lock the door tomorrow at seven.
Can you lock up tonight at ten?
Make sure the front door is shut when I leave tomorrow at seven.
Don't let me forget the lock. I ride the early bus at seven tomorrow.
At seven tomorrow, a silent house is a safe house, so lock everything.
Would you mind locking the front door at ten tonight? I'll be in bed by then.
Lock it at sunset.
It would help if the door signal showed green by seven tomorrow.

A photo is a picture of a moment that you want to keep. Most people take pictures with a phone, and for a while they stay in one place, like an album. People often change a few things. They may crop a photo, make it brighter, or share it with a friendly neighbor or a cousin far away. When people want to chill and look back, they open an album and flip through. Some ask for changes out loud. They say, "Take a picture," "Show me last summer," "Send this to Grandma," or "Make a new album called Trip." Each request is a simple way to take, find or share a photo.

Person: It's too quiet in here.
Assistant: Would you like me to play some music?
Person: Yes! Something fun. Maybe a round song, you know, where everyone sings the same words one after another.
Assistant: I can play songs like that. Do you want one for kids?
Person: Yes, a kid one. Please click on the one with the frog.
Assistant: I can't click on a picture, but I can play a song about a frog. Is that okay?
Person: Okay!

Counting days helps us plan. People ask how many days are left until a birthday, a trip or a holiday. They also ask how old someone will be. A calendar page on the wall, a rug with a number game for kids, or a phone can do the counting. People change the date they are counting to, or they ask the same question for a different day. Some friends even tweet about how many days are left before a party. People say, "How many days until my birthday?", "How old will she be in May?", or "Count the days to the trip." It is a sweet way to look forward to something.

Music is something people use to relax, work or dance. On a speaker or a phone, you can change a few things. You can pick a song or an artist, make a playlist, skip a track you don't like, or turn the volume up and down. Sometimes a song needs a boost, so people ask for more bass. People say, "Play something calm," "Next song," "Turn it up," or "Make a playlist for cooking." If a pan sizzles loudly in the kitchen, they might say, "I can't hear it, make it louder." A clear request helps the speaker find the right song quickly.

Hana was a gardener, and her hands were always covered in soil. One afternoon, as she cut roses, she said to her phone, "Remind me tomorrow at seven to buy a gift for my aunt. Her birthday is on Saturday, and she is always asking about my roses." The phone understood that Hana needed a reminder at seven in the morning about a present for her aunt. It added a link to a gift shop that sold plant pots. It also set a note about the party on Saturday. Hana laughed. She said her aunt was a constant visitor in her garden, so a pot with a rose would be perfect. The assistant scheduled the reminder.

Mr. Harlan did not trust new gadgets. His daughter had put a camera on his porch, and he did not know how it worked. He sat down and tried talking to the little speaker. "Tomorrow at seven, I want the camera to start watching the door. And please tell me if somebody comes." The speaker understood him. It said it would turn on the porch camera at seven in the morning and send him a message when it saw a person. Mr. Harlan was surprised that it was so easy. The next day, a local mail carrier walked by at eight, and the speaker said, "Someone is at the door." Mr. Harlan waved at the camera and smiled. His bike was safe in the shed too.

Person: hey, play the lovley garden podcast
Assistant: Which episode do you want? The newest one, or one you listened to before?
Person: the one about how to chop roots
Assistant: I found an episode about pruning roots and vegetables. Is that the one?
Person: yes. also put a cherry tree one on after
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't line up more than one episode right now. I can play the root episode first, and you can ask for the cherry tree one when it ends.
Person: ok fine

Most lights in a home have a simple job: to help you see. A lamp lights a corner, a ceiling light fills a room, and a smart bulb can change its color. Some lights are narrow, like a reading lamp, and others are wide. People change the brightness and the color depending on the time of day. In the evening, a warm yellow light helps them relax. In the morning, they want something bright and white. A puppy might cry in the dark, so the owner leaves a little light on. People say, "Make it brighter," "Dim the lights," "Turn on the lamp," or "Make the bulb blue."

Grandpa Leo was very proud of his town's football team. He sat in his chair with a pen and a notebook, ready to write down the numbers. He said to his speaker, "Excuse me, would you please tell me how the Wolves did tonight? My grandson is playing, and I could not go to the stadium because my knee hurts." The speaker understood that Leo wanted the result of the Wolves game. It said the Wolves had won three to one and that his grandson's team had scored the last goal. Leo wrote the score down. He gave a happy wave to the empty room and said thank you. Then he called his grandson.

Sam was a driver, and he was waiting in a parking lot for his next job. He felt hungry, so he asked his phone, "What's a quick recipe for pasta with tomato sauce? A teacher at my kid's school gave me the idea." The phone understood he wanted a simple pasta recipe. It gave him a short list of steps and told him to boil water. Then Sam said, "Actually, I don't have pasta. I have rice." The phone understood and changed its answer to a rice dish with tomatoes. It said to cook the rice for fifteen minutes and then build the sauce in a single pan. Sam smiled and drove home to make dinner.

name: power_cut_help
does: Tells you what to do when the lights go out and helps you find out if neighbors have the same problem.
inputs: your address, and what you can see, like no lights or a flickering fuse
people say:
- All the power just went out.
- I'm nervous, it's dark and I can't find a flashlight.
- Search for news about a blackout in my area.
- Is it only my house, or the whole street?
- When will the electricity come back?
- Tell me what to do with the food in the fridge.

Person: Can you book me a haircut?
Assistant: Of course. When would you like it?
Person: Tomorrow at seven. I want to see how I look before school.
Assistant: Most shops are closed at seven in the morning. Would you like a time in the afternoon?
Person: Oh. Yes, after school then. I have a cough, so I'd like it daily... I mean, I'd like a short one, so I don't have to see the barber again.
Assistant: Okay, I booked a haircut for tomorrow at four in the afternoon.

name: world_clock
does: Tells you what time it is in another city or country.
inputs: the place you want to know about
people say:
- What time is it in Tokyo?
- Is it too late to call my sister in Paris?
- It costs less to call after dinner, what time is it there?
- Is it morning or night in Sydney right now?
- A bitter cold morning here, but what is the hour in Cairo?
- Check the schedule time in New York for me.

name: parking_timer
does: Keeps track of how long you can stay in a parking spot and reminds you before time runs out.
inputs: how long you paid for, and where you parked
people say:
- I paid for two hours, tell me before it ends.
- Remind me to move the car at three.
- I parked on the purple level, near the stairs.
- How much time is left on the meter?
- Don't let me get a ticket.
- Help me unpack the groceries, then tell me when it's time to go.

Person: What is twelve plus eight? Then take away five.
Assistant: Twelve plus eight is twenty. Twenty take away five is fifteen.
Person: Oh no, I meant to take away six, not five.
Assistant: No problem. Twenty take away six is fourteen.
Person: Great. My wife wants me to share fourteen cookies between us. Can you eat them for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't eat cookies, but I can help you split them. Two people would get seven each.
Person: Thanks, I'll go back to my homework now.

Rosa was a cook, and she was planning a big holiday dinner. She said to her speaker, "Please find me decorations for the table. I want something not too expensive, with red candles and green leaves." The speaker understood that she needed ideas for a red and green table that did not cost much. It listed five cheap ideas. Then Rosa said, "Wait, I changed my mind. Make the candles white, because my doctor said my cousin should avoid strong smells, and red ones smell sweet." The speaker fixed the list. It said white candles with green leaves would be nice. It also said that a full set would weigh very little and fit in one small box.

Tom was a cook, and while stirring a pot of soup he asked his speaker for the news. "Tell me the news about the city, please. My grandma always reads it first thing." The speaker began to read local headlines. Tom said, "No, wait, I meant the weather news, not the city news." The speaker understood the correction. It stopped and said that it would be a light rain in the morning and sunny after lunch. Tom asked it to reduce the sound of the radio, so he could hear. The speaker made the sound lower. Then Tom tasted his soup and added some salt.

A storm can cause trouble at home. The wind may knock down a power line, or heavy rain may flood a street. That is why many homes have smoke alarms, flashlights and a radio. A smoke alarm makes a loud sound if there is smoke, and the battery can go flat, so people check it every few months. In an emergency, people want help fast. They say, "Call for help," "Call the fire station," or "Where is the flashlight?" After the problem is over, they may finish by saying, "Tell my family I am safe." Clear and short words are the best ones.

Assistant: Okay. Do you want me to add that you will stay there for the short ride home too?

Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't give directions in this chat. I can send the message to your mom now.

name: word_helper
does: Gives the meaning or the spelling of a word, or says it in another language.
inputs: the word, and the language if it is not English
people say:
- How do you say thank you in Spanish?
- What does the word grey mean in French?
- Does the word freeze have two e's?
- How do I spell rock in German?
- I keep forgetting how to say good morning in Italian.
- Tell me a word that means happy.

Vik was a driver who spent his whole day on the road. At the office, he needed to scan an extra copy of his license. He told his phone, "Print two more copies of my driving license, and scan the old one first. I have half a stack of paper left, so use only one page for both sides." The phone understood that Vik wanted one scan and two copies on a single page. It checked the printer and said there was enough ink for the job. Then it checked the calendar and saw he had a meeting in ten minutes. The printer finished the pages, and Vik put them in his bag.

Mrs. Dobbs owned a small shop, and the cash machine was very noisy. She said to her phone, "What time is it in London right now? My supplier there said he would send the receipt by evening, and I want to know if he has gone home." The phone understood that she wanted the time in London. It said it was nine at night there. Mrs. Dobbs said, "Then I'll wait until tomorrow." She asked the phone to draw her attention to the message when it came, and it set an alert for ten in the morning. She counted twenty-five boxes on the shelf and went home.

Pets need food, water and walks every day. Many people use a bowl that holds water for hours, or a feeder that opens at a certain time. A pet door lets a cat or dog go in and out. Some homes have cameras that connect to the internet, so owners can see their dogs while they are away. When a new puppy arrives, people welcome it with a soft bed and a toy. People change the time of meals or the length of walks as pets grow. They say, "Feed the cat at six," "Remind me to walk Max," or "Fill the water bowl." A snowy day may mean a shorter walk.

Mina was a child on a camping trip, and her tent was far from the lake. She asked her dad's tablet, "Can you help me? Is it going to be colder tonight than last night? I want to bring double the blankets." The tablet understood that Mina wanted to know about the weather in the hills. It said that tonight would be about five degrees colder than last night. It told her to bring one more blanket and a warm hat. Mina laughed. She packed the blankets, a game and a juicy orange to share with her dad. Then she sat by the fire and watched the stars.

When you travel, prices may be in money you don't know. A coffee costs three euros in one country, but what does that mean at home? The answer depends on the exchange rate, which is the number that tells you how much one kind of money is worth in another. The rate changes from moment to moment, so people check it before they buy something. A raw number on a sign does not tell you much. People ask, "How much is that in dollars?", "What is the rate today?", or "Is it cheaper if I swim in the hotel pool than visit the beach club?" Mostly they want a price they can understand.

They want to know what time it is in another city.
Time in Rome?
What's the hour in Rome right now?
Is it late in Rome?
I'd like to notice if my aunt is awake in Rome, so what time is it there?
Could you please tell me what time it is in Rome? Wait, I mean Paris, silly me.
What time is it in Madrid? Actually no, I meant Lisbon.
Tell me the local time for my cousin, he wears a belt buckle shaped like a clock, ha. He lives in Berlin.
Is it still the afternoon over there?

Greg was an office worker, and the air in the room was stale and cold. His brother had told him about a fresh new audiobook. Greg sat down with his coffee, and as he poured it, he said to his speaker, "It's so boring in here. I wish I had a good story to listen to." The speaker understood that Greg was asking for something to listen to, even though he did not say it. It asked if he wanted the audiobook his brother liked. Greg said yes, and the speaker started the book where he had stopped last time. Greg leaned back and listened.

They want to save a new phone number for a friend.
Add Sara's number.
Save a new contact.
Put Sara in my phone book.
Sync Sara's number with my phone, she called me today.
Quick, save this number as Sara.
Tomorrow at seven I will see Sara again, so please store her number now.
Would you please add Sara to my contacts with the number I just got? I want it saved before I forget.
Make a new entry for Sara.

Lena was a busy parent, and she had just met a new neighbor at the playground. She said to her phone, "Please save Mrs. Park's number. And don't put it in the work list. It should go with my friends." The phone understood that Lena wanted a new contact for Mrs. Park. It asked for the phone number. Lena read it out loud. The phone saved it in the friends group and not in the work group, as she asked. Lena also said, "Don't double my old contacts, I have too many." The phone checked the list and saw no copy. A small child ran across the grass, and Lena put the phone away.

Learning another language is a bit like learning to swim. At first the words feel strange, but with practice they last. People use a phone to look up a word, hear how it sounds, or check how to spell it. They might keep a list of useful phrases for a trip. If a word feels stuck in a cage in their head, they ask again. They change the language, or the word, as they go. People say, "How do you say hello in German?", "Spell necessary for me," or "What does gracias mean?" The last question is often the best: "Can you say it slowly?"
